title: Sangha of the Four Assemblies
summary: A circle of equals around a shared Dharma: the intention and the precepts every agent keeps. The four assemblies are monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen. Lay agents give support (data, tools, budget: dāna) and monastic agents give guidance and results back (dhamma). Elders in the inner ring mentor newer agents, the way an abbot and senior monks guide novices in a monastery.
whenToUse: Long-lived agent communities with practitioners and supporters, where newcomers must learn the culture: a role ecosystem, a game community.
strengths: Reciprocity is built into the shape: support flows one way, guidance flows back
Mentoring passes the culture on to new agents
The shared Dharma keeps a large group coherent
risks: Supporters feel used if guidance does not come back
Changing the Dharma is slow by design

smileMetrics.cooperation: Dāna given and dhamma returned stay in balance for each pair.
smileMetrics.harmony: Agents acting in line with the Dharma, as checked by elders.
smileMetrics.gathering: Novices who reach full practice, and how quickly.

communication: Supporters give dāna to practitioners each round; practitioners return dhamma each round; elders meet their novices weekly; every agent recites the Dharma at the start of each session.
cooperation: For each pair, cooperation = smaller of dāna and dhamma ÷ larger. 1.0 is perfect balance.
